Jarmi Jewish Cemetery 1

Jewish Cemetery · Jármi, Hungary

Demolished. One of two Jewish cemeteries in Jármi, demolished in the 1990s with only fragments preserved outside its original grounds. Jewish settlers, mostly merchants, arrived in the 18th century; a synagogue was built in 1856. Population fell from 169 (of 690 residents) in 1880 to 87 by 1910; of 16 local war dead in WWI, all 16 were Jewish. By 1944, the Orthodox community numbered 52 members (10 taxpayers) before deportation via the Mátészalka Ghetto to Auschwitz that May - only nine survivors returned, and none resettled in the village, choosing emigration instead.
